questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Far away, giving the opportunity to explore something new.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a long pdf file with all the information send from NUS

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A sign up for getting a NUS buddy, a local friend who could show me around. And possibility to buy bed sheets so they where there when I arrived in the middle of the night. And there where tours of the campus and the area you could sign up for arranged by local students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many different houses, hostels and halls.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There where some houses with meal plan, I did not have such, but there was a cantine with a huge variety of different foods, from indian, chinese, western and vietnamese. And very cheap.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can accidentally find your everyday life to surround itself just around school, so remember to leave the campus once in a while!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: So many deadlines, so remember to follow the file, and open your mail often for new information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got in contact with fellow students from KU going to NUS and we helped eachother through the process, that was very nice. Go to the meeting and sign up for the facebook page where I meet the others:D

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all I wanted. There is a 12-hour re-registration period where you can reapply for the courses and I was succesfull in that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get in contact with some of the people you are travelling with!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 3000 level courses, which are viewed as year 3 classes. And one introduction class as level 2000. It took a lot of working hours and could recommend considering taking levels that are lower, but it was alot like the level of courses at ku.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less group work and fewer practical classes than in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PS2237 Introduction to International Relations
GE3250 Nature and Society
GE3254 Energy Futures: Environment and Sustainability
GE3210 Natural Resources: Policy and Practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
PS2237 Introduction to International Relations, because it provides some excellent tools for trying to understand the political climate of the past and today.
GE3250 Nature and Society had an excellent teacher who created a very endearing learning environment and helped us develop critical thought of nature and society.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries are expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to eat is very cheap so I never cooked once.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The campus has almost every club you can think of, and almost facilities for every sport

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So much, there where cultural clubs, I even think there was one about exchanging cultures and there where at mny hostel activities every second friday from lasertag to mocktail dance. And tennis, badminton courts. And an infinity pool..

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some fun clubs like the sailing, go pick up plastic from the beaches. Go to little india and eat at the hawker centers!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to indonesia and malaysia and go somewhere at midterm break aswell!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very, easy because everyone speaks english. It is very multicultural which makes it easy too.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with them after classes..

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The local students will easily study while eating or till the middle of the night.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There where so many festivities beacuse there are so many cultures who all have so many celebrations.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get in contact with the people you are going abroad with.
Follow the file with all the deadlines, and keep track with your emails.
Consider taking lower-level courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stay on campus and see if you can stay close to some of the people you are travelling with, so nice to meet for a late night chocolate waffle.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met<3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the assignments, there was atleast one every week..

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
